target_customer: Airlines handling passengers stranded by flight disruptions
problem: Airlines scramble to find hotel rooms for disrupted passengers. Roomstorm connects airlines directly to hotel inventory in real time.
business_model: B2B marketplace take rate on hotel bookings for airlines (not stated by sources)

founders.name: Maksim Izmaylov
founders.background_notes: Per YC page. CB Insights snippet names Jakub Vysoky as CTO, not stated as co-founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed airline and hotel inventory integrations and real time booking automation.

defensibility.rationale: Airline integrations create some stickiness but hotel supply and connectors can be replicated.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No dated incumbent action found; the company launched Stormy AI passenger care platform per a LinkedIn post.

market_need_then: Disrupted passenger hotel handling was a manual airline process; a July 2014 Norwegian Air case at LAX is an example of the pain, but is not a Roomstorm source.

rebrands.why: CB Insights lists WalkSource as the former name; date and reason not found

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand; storm metaphor fits disruption use case but only trade press found.

outcome_analysis: Roomstorm remains a small Prague based B2B company focused on airline disruption bookings, with a four person team per YC and a newer AI product called Stormy. Public evidence of traction or large funding is thin, so its outcome is a niche survivor with unclear scale.
notes: Funding sources conflict and are aggregators only: CB Insights 1.22M across three rounds with 120K on 2014-08-20 including YC, PitchBook 120K accelerator 2014-08-19 and seed January 2015, StartupIntros 1M seed 2015-05-01 with Esther Dyson and Adora Cheung, another source 2.4M total. None confirmed by press so no round recorded. Company site had no content. PhocusWire page could not be fetched (403).
